title: Twenty First Word First Station Fifth Warning Two Spiritual Mines And The Loss Of Abandoning Prayer

questions.question: What is the first special gain a gardener can receive if the gardener works with a good intention?
questions.answer: The gardener can share in the reward of the worship made by the plants and trees he grows.

questions.question: What kinds of plants are included in that first gain?
questions.answer: It includes both kinds: those with blossoms and those that produce fruit.

questions.question: What is the second special gain connected to the garden’s produce?
questions.answer: Whatever is eaten from it can count like charity for the gardener.

questions.question: Which eaters are mentioned to show how wide this reward can be?
questions.answer: It includes people, animals, farm animals, flies, customers, and even thieves.

questions.question: What two conditions are needed for that eating to count like charity from the gardener?
questions.answer: The gardener must work for Allah’s sake and stay within what Allah allows.

questions.question: How should the gardener think about his role with the garden’s produce?
questions.answer: He should see himself as a trusted worker handing out Allah’s property to His creatures.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does a person lose by leaving the required prayers?
questions.answer: He loses great spiritual riches and misses the two valuable gains.

questions.question: How does losing those gains affect a person’s energy and attitude?
questions.answer: It weakens his desire to work and lowers his spirit.

questions.question: What may happen to such a person when he becomes older?
questions.answer: He may get tired of gardening, stop caring, and become lazy.

questions.question: What kind of thinking leads him into that laziness?
questions.answer: He thinks he will leave this world anyway, so he feels the hard work is not worth it.

questions.question: How is the other man different in his response?
questions.answer: He chooses to work more in worship and in lawful work.

questions.question: Why does the other man want to work harder?
questions.answer: He wants to send more light to his grave and prepare more for the life to come.

questions.question: In the passage, what does having a sound intention do for someone working in a garden?
questions.answer: It turns ordinary gardening into a way to gain reward.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect a person with the praise made by plants and trees?
questions.answer: Because the person helped grow them with the right intention.

questions.question: How does the passage show that even small creatures matter in reward?
questions.answer: It says that even when flies eat from the garden, it can still bring reward.

questions.question: Why are even thieves mentioned among those who may eat the produce?
questions.answer: To show that the reward can still reach the gardener very broadly, not just in easy or expected situations.

questions.question: What mistake would a gardener make if he thought the produce fully belonged to him in an absolute way?
questions.answer: He would forget that it is really Allah’s provision and that he is only handling it as a servant.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about lawful work and worship?
questions.answer: They should go together, not be separated.

questions.question: What does the word “bankrupt” suggest about the one who leaves prayer?
questions.answer: It suggests that he ends up spiritually poor and empty.

questions.question: What emotional result comes to the prayerless person over time?
questions.answer: He becomes discouraged and loses the will to continue.

questions.question: What future-focused goal gives the other man strength?
questions.answer: He wants benefit for his grave and the hereafter.

questions.question: Which man is more likely to keep good morale, and why?
questions.answer: The praying man, because he sees deeper reward and purpose in his work.

questions.question: What work setting is used in the passage to teach a lesson?
questions.answer: A garden and the work done in it.

questions.question: What is the first “mine” really about?
questions.answer: It is about gaining hidden spiritual reward through sincere intention.

questions.question: What is the second “mine” really about?
questions.answer: It is about the garden’s produce becoming like charity when used in the right way.

questions.question: What must be true about a person’s purpose for the first gain to happen?
questions.answer: The person’s purpose must be sound and sincere.

questions.question: What must be true about a person’s actions for the second gain to happen?
questions.answer: The person must act within Allah’s allowed limits.

questions.question: What picture does the passage give of a human being’s place in providing food?
questions.answer: A human is not the true owner but a servant passing on Allah’s provision.

questions.question: If someone gives up the required prayers, what two benefits does he miss?
questions.answer: He misses sharing in the reward tied to the plants and the charity-like reward tied to the produce.

questions.question: What does the passage say these two benefits would have done for him?
questions.answer: They would have made him eager to work and helped him stay strong in spirit.

questions.question: How does old age affect the person who leaves prayer in this passage?
questions.answer: It makes his weariness and loss of interest even worse.

questions.question: What words show that this person’s problem is not only physical tiredness?
questions.answer: He also loses heart and falls into idleness.

questions.question: What two kinds of effort does the better example combine?
questions.answer: Worship and lawful worldly effort.

questions.question: What turns growing plants into something more than just farming or gardening?
questions.answer: A good intention for Allah turns it into rewarded service.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the value of feeding others from one’s work?
questions.answer: It can bring the reward of charity.

questions.question: Does the passage limit this benefit only to people who buy the produce fairly?
questions.answer: No. The benefit is described much more widely, including many kinds of eaters.

questions.question: What protects a person from misunderstanding this wide reward?
questions.answer: The reminder that the person must work for Allah and stay within what Allah permits.

questions.question: Why is it important that the gardener sees himself as a distribution worker, not an absolute owner?
questions.answer: It helps him stay humble and remember that the provision belongs to Allah.

questions.question: What happens inside a person when he abandons the prescribed prayers, according to the passage?
questions.answer: He suffers a big inner loss and becomes spiritually empty.

questions.question: How does this inner loss affect his work life?
questions.answer: He no longer works with joy or strong motivation.

questions.question: What kind of sentence shows that the tired man has become hopeless about worldly life?
questions.answer: He thinks leaving the world soon means the effort is not worth continuing.

questions.question: What is the connection between hope in the hereafter and energy in this world?
questions.answer: Hope in the hereafter gives a person more strength to work well in this world.

questions.question: How does the second man view hard work differently?
questions.answer: He sees it as a way to prepare for what comes after death.

questions.question: Who is the true giver of provision in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah is the true giver of provision.

questions.question: What should a worker remember about the food or produce he handles?
questions.answer: He should remember that it belongs to Allah, not to him in an absolute sense.

questions.question: When can eating from the garden become like charity from the worker?
questions.answer: When the worker acts for Allah’s sake and follows Allah’s lawful limits.

questions.question: Why is a good intention so important in the passage?
questions.answer: It changes normal work into worshipful reward.

questions.question: What part do trees and plants play in the worker’s reward?
questions.answer: Their acts of praise become a source of shared reward for him.

questions.question: What shows that the reward is not just for special religious moments?
questions.answer: The passage shows reward can come during everyday garden work.

questions.question: What does the passage say is lost by a person who stops the required prayers?
questions.answer: He loses major spiritual wealth and the two precious gains.

questions.question: How is that loss described in a strong way?
questions.answer: The person is described as becoming like someone ruined in wealth.

questions.question: What change may happen in his feelings as he gets older?
questions.answer: He may become more tired, uninterested, and lazy.

questions.question: What wrong conclusion does the lazy person reach about life?
questions.answer: He decides there is no point in bearing hardship since he will leave the world.

questions.question: What better conclusion does the other man reach?
questions.answer: He decides to increase both worship and lawful effort.

questions.question: What reward does the second man hope to increase by doing that?
questions.answer: He hopes for more light in the grave and more provision for the next life.

questions.question: What example is used to explain how ordinary work can bring reward?
questions.answer: The example of working in a garden is used.

questions.question: What is promised to the one who grows plants with the right intention?
questions.answer: He gains spiritual reward connected to the worship of what he grows.

questions.question: What does the passage say about produce eaten by many different kinds of creatures and people?
questions.answer: It can count like charity from the worker.

questions.question: What must guide the worker’s actions for this reward to be valid?
questions.answer: He must work for Allah and stay within what Allah allows.

questions.question: What attitude about ownership is the worker told to have?
questions.answer: He should think of himself as a servant delivering Allah’s gifts.

questions.question: What is the effect of abandoning the required prayers on these two “mines”?
questions.answer: The person is cut off from their benefits.

questions.question: Besides missing reward, what personal weakness develops in that person?
questions.answer: His morale becomes weak.

questions.question: What long-term result may show up in his work habits?
questions.answer: He may lose interest and stop wanting to work.

questions.question: What does his complaint about leaving the world show about his thinking?
questions.answer: It shows he sees only this worldly life and not the lasting life ahead.

questions.question: How does the other man’s view of work show stronger faith?
questions.answer: He links his work to worship, the grave, and the hereafter.

questions.question: Which kind of activities does the other man want to increase?
questions.answer: He wants to increase acts of worship and lawful daily work.

questions.question: If you compare the two men, what makes the second one stronger inside?
questions.answer: He has purpose, hope in the hereafter, and a worshipful intention.
